features.description: Write all regression tests before the fix: Scheme-level unit tests in internal/types/ plus two-module cross-module fixtures in internal/pipeline/. Both RED tests must be observed failing for the right reason, and both GREEN tests must pass at base so they cannot pass vacuously.
acceptance_criteria: internal/types/effect_row_defaulting_test.go exists with three cases: recursive pure binding asserts RowVars empty and a closed effect row (RED at base); declared ! {e} binding asserts RowVars == [e] preserved (GREEN at base, pins V14); recursive ! {IO} binding asserts closed {IO} (GREEN at base, pins V9)

internal/pipeline/validate_effects_xmod_test.go exists with two two-module fixtures: accept case reproducing the #1091 shape (pure export delegating to a private recursive scan, imported by a pure function reachable from an ! {FS} function) failing at base with exactly 'Missing effects: FS' (RED); reject case where an importer calls a genuinely ! {IO} cross-module function from a pure function and is still rejected (GREEN at base)
The RED cross-module test fails with 'Missing effects: FS', NOT with a type error — a type error means the fixture does not reproduce the defect
All assertions are on the types.Scheme (TypeVars/RowVars/Type), never on 'ailang iface' output, which flattens the row variable away and reports a row-polymorphic export as pure:true (design doc V16)
go test ./internal/types/... ./internal/pipeline/... runs and shows exactly the two expected failures and no others
features.notes: Done, consolidated into ONE file internal/pipeline/effect_pure_row_overgeneralization_test.go (7 tests) instead of the two planned files. A pure internal/types unit test cannot observe this defect: the declared row is not an input to generalizeWithConstraints, so the assertion must be made after the module interface is built (pipeline layer), on Result.Interface.Exports[...].Type. The RED test failed for the stated reason (RowVars=[rho2] on `pure func hLast`), and four control tests passed at base so none is vacuous.

features.description: Add effect-row defaulting before generalization: when a top-level binding's declared effect row is closed, bind its unresolved effect-row variables to that declared row so no compiler-fresh row var is quantified into the exported scheme. Keyed on the declaration, never on the row variable's name.
acceptance_criteria: Effect-row defaulting runs alongside the existing type-class defaulting pass in the LetRec path (internal/types/typechecker_functions.go:330-377) and the corresponding Let/top-level binding path, before generalizeWithConstraints

The discriminator is the binding's DECLARED effect row, not the row variable's name prefix: a closed declared row (pure, no ! annotation, or an explicit closed ! {...}) closes the inferred row; a declared row carrying a user-written row variable bound in the signature's type params is left polymorphic
Only unresolved effect-row VARIABLES are defaulted — concrete labels are never removed, so a genuine effect still reaches the effect checker
All M1 tests green, including both previously-GREEN pins
DEBUG_EFFECTS=1 on the reconstructed repro reports 'VarGlobal(docparse/services/pkg_template.pkgLastIndexOf) -> []'
No existing effect-checking test's expected message text is changed
make test and make lint green
features.notes: Done in internal/types/effect_row_declared_closure.go (new) wired into both generalization paths in typechecker_functions.go. NARROWER than the design doc specified: closure applies only when the outer row variable occurs nowhere else in the type. The doc's whole-type substitution was wrong - an inferred row shared with a callback is load-bearing even with no `! {e}` (std/list.flatMap), and closing it broke epub_parser's flatMap call with 'incompatible closed rows: r1 [] vs r2 [FS]'. Discriminator is the declaration (ast.EffectAnnotation.IsRowVar / isEffectRowVar), never the row-variable name.
